places.marsh: The origin is the centre of the seep pool. North is -z and east is +x. The world is a salt flat 18 km square inside a ring of escarpment that starts about 5 km out, and fog hides the far edge. The establishing eye stands 8.5 m above the flats on a rock rise about 7 m high and looks 52 degrees east of north, with the pool 35 m ahead and 15 m to its left.
places.heart: The origin is the middle of the caldera floor on the surface of the lake. North is -z, toward the far wall and the vessel mouth, and east is +x, toward the buttress and the second chamber. The world is 12 km square. The floor is about 2.4 km by 0.85 km, the main chamber is about 1 km from the bench to the far wall, and the walls stand 300 m. The tall ones are 9 to 15 m high at the back. The establishing eye is 25 m above the lake on the bench ledge and looks 49 degrees east of north.
places.breath: The origin is the centre of the main shaft at the level of the shelf. North is -z and east is +x. The world is 16 km square. The shaft is 60 m across and 70 m deep, with its collapse on the east and south east side. The cliff with the cave is about 3 km away to the north east and the sun is low in the north. Every key looks north to north north east, so the cliff is upper right and the sun upper left. The waders are about 3.4 m tall.
places.eye: The origin is the centre of the lake, on the water. North is -z and east is +x. The low sun is in the west. The world is a disc 3.4 km in radius. The shore is 1 km from the centre, so the lake is 2 km across, and the deep is a disc 480 m in radius. The cliffs stand about 200 m, lower in the west and the south, with the brow overhanging on the east. A gravel fan brings the south shore in by 180 m, and the herd stands on it. The drinkers are about 3.3 m to the head.
places.ribs: The origin is on the floor of the strait between the first pair of ribs, level with the drowned one. North is -z, down the strait, where the bore comes from, and east is +x. Sea level is 0. The tidal floor is a plateau 1460 m from east to west and 3430 m from north to south, about 1 m above the sea. There are 13 ribs in two rows 600 to 800 m apart, 280 to 520 m high and leaning in, with two outer ribs to seaward for the opening. The weed line is at 30 m. The bore is one wall 28 m high.
places.spine: The origin is the foot of the first spire, on its axis. The ridge runs toward +x. The storm is on the -z side and the cloud sea and the last light are on the +z side. There are 16 vertebrae along a curved line, with spires about 800 m apart and fins 230 to 300 m above their saddles. The cloud sea lies 2000 m below. The mouth of the canal sits 46 m to the lee of the crest and 120 m before the first spire, 20 m in radius, narrowing to a throat 8 m across. The canal runs through the first vertebra: it enters at the mouth seen from outside, 46 m to the lee of the crest and 120 m before the first spire, and leaves 232 m further along the ridge, on the lee side past the first spire, by a far mouth 13 m in radius. Shot spine-05 is filmed near that far mouth.

reveal-01.start: Deep water and nine pale rings, seen from straight above the centre of the lake, 20 km of water above and below the middle of the frame. The last frames of the Eye draw the same water and the same rings at the same rate of climb, so the cut cannot be seen. The amber shore enters the frame after about 0.8 s and the rings fade into the water as it does.
reveal-01.end: The whole body lies in the frame from the skull to the feet, with the edge of the planet across the top and the cyclone at the lower right. The window of the approved picture is reached on the titan frame, 10027. The camera does not stop there: it eases down to a steady crawl and keeps pulling back until the cut to black, 22 percent wider by then, and it drifts until the middle of the body is the middle of the frame, with clear sea on every side.
reveal-01.move: It is one rise straight up, with north at the top. It leaves the lake at the rate of climb the Eye ends on, is fastest as the shore of the lake fills the frame, and slows through the skull and the shoulders to the titan frame. In the hold the clouds drift east, the cyclone turns, the storm flickers and the Heart beats once, on the music's last strike at frame 11334.
reveal-01.focus: On the ground straight below, at every height.

marsh-01.start: From 9 m behind the key position and about 3 m above it, over the rock rise: the whole marsh, with the pool on the left, the red vein running from the bottom centre to the upper right, the crust and its dead on the right, rain on the right and a flock crossing the sky.
marsh-01.end: 12 m ahead of the key position and lower, past the rise and over the vein, with the pool on the left and the wallowers in the vein ahead.
marsh-01.focus: On the pool and the vein beside it.

marsh-02.start: Inside the stalk colony on the south west bank of the pool, 2.7 m up, with stems and fans crossing the foreground.
marsh-02.end: 6.4 m to the right, past the four tall stems of the key picture, the view opens onto the pool with one wallower on its far bank.
marsh-02.focus: On the four tall stems, a few metres from the lens. The wallower beyond them is soft.

marsh-03.start: On the south rim of the pool about 1 m up, 2.2 m behind the key position, looking across the surface at the largest gas dome.
marsh-03.end: About 3.8 m from the column of the burst and outside it, turned 8 degrees and tilted up 7, with the column and its crown filling the frame.
marsh-03.focus: On the largest dome, then on the column that rises from it at the burst.

marsh-04.start: Over the vein at 2.7 m, on the adult rooting in the brine with the young beside it and a half sunk one in front.
marsh-04.end: 5.9 m to the left and lower, at 2.05 m, on the same three animals, with stalks crossing the foreground.
marsh-04.focus: On the head and forelimbs of the adult.

marsh-05.start: 12 m back from the key position and about 2.6 m above it, over the crust: the stuck one small in the frame with the salt mounds of the dead on either side.
marsh-05.end: 1.7 m past the key position at about 1.3 m, close on the stuck one, with stalks and wallowers behind it.
marsh-05.focus: On the head of the stuck one.

heart-01.start: From 29 m behind the key position and 3 m above it, over the bench: the whole lake, with the vessel mouth and the lava fall upper left, the buttress and its plume on the right, the bench lower left and the tall ones on the crust.
heart-01.end: 29 m ahead of the key position and 17 m above the lake, off the edge of the bench, with the nearest of the tall ones large on the left of the frame and the one that sank beyond it.
heart-01.move: One push of 59 m toward the mouth with a slight crab to the right, down from 28 m to 17 m, through the establishing view at the key frame. The bench falls away under the lens and the lake opens.
heart-01.focus: On the nearest of the tall ones.

heart-02.start: 6.6 m over the crust and 74 m from the hero of the group on a long lens: the hero left of centre with its trunk down in the seam, the second of the group walking on the right, a third far off on the left in front of the fall, the mouth at the left edge.
heart-02.end: 16 m closer and a little lower, the same heading, with the hero two thirds of the height of the frame.
heart-02.move: One push of 16 m toward the hero, with a metre of crab to the right. The lens stays about 6 m over the crust, so the hero's back stands at twice the height of the lens.
heart-02.focus: On the hero of the group.

heart-03.start: 2.7 m up on the last rocks of the shore: the crag and the steaming sulphur vent on the left, the glowing channel leaving the shore ahead and crossing the frame to the lower right, the mouth and the fall upper left, the tall ones upper right.
heart-03.end: 7 m further and 1.6 m up, at the edge of the shore, with the channel just below the lens.
heart-03.move: One push of 7 m toward the mouth with a slight crab to the right, down from 2.7 m to 1.6 m, slowing onto the channel.
heart-03.focus: On the channel, a few metres ahead of the lens.

heart-04.start: 4.9 m over the crust, 24 m from the one that sank: the carcass in the middle, the nearest of the tall ones feeding on the left, the mouth and the fall behind it, the buttress on the right.
heart-04.end: 5.5 m closer and a little lower, the same heading.
heart-04.move: One slow push of 5.5 m toward the carcass with a slight crab to the right.

heart-05.start: 777 m from the vessel mouth and 2.5 m over the crust, on the longest lens of the place: the mouth, the whole fall and its foot.
heart-05.end: 34 m closer and 3.8 m over the crust, still aimed at the same point beside the mouth, with the surge running down the fall.
heart-05.move: One push of 34 m toward the mouth with a slight crab to the right and a small rise. On this lens the wall hardly grows; the near crust slides under the frame. The surge comes at frame 4010.
heart-05.focus: On the mouth and the fall, through the whole push.

breath-01.start: From about 34 m behind the key position and 2 m above it, over the channel: the tide channel from lower left to centre, the shaft right of centre with its fallen slabs, the wader at the rim, the cliff and its cave upper right, the sun upper left and the far herd on the flats.
breath-01.end: 49 m further on, just past the key position, 9 m above the shelf, with the shaft and its rim larger on the right.
breath-01.focus: On the rim of the shaft.

breath-02.start: On the south rim of the shaft, 9 m behind the key position: the hoops down the north wall, the fallen slabs and the weed on the left.
breath-02.end: 17 m ahead and 1.9 m higher, tilted 6 degrees down into the shaft. The breath has risen above the rim: it begins at frame 4652 and stands about 20 m high near the end of the shot.
breath-02.focus: On the north wall and its hoops, then on the rising column.

breath-03.start: Close on the largest weed on the west lip, 3.5 m in front of the key position.
breath-03.end: 10.5 m back: the weed, the breath pouring west over the lip, and the channel and the waders behind.

breath-04.start: 1.9 m above the bed of the channel, on three waders with the cliff behind them: the near one with its neck down on the left.
breath-04.end: 13 m to the right and 5 m forward, past the three.

breath-05.start: On the shelf south west of the rim: the dead wader in the foreground, the wader at the rim feeding behind it, the weed, the shaft and its slabs on the right, the cliff upper right.
breath-05.end: 11.5 m closer, low over the dead wader.

eye-01.start: 88 m behind the key position and 37 m above the water, over the gravel fan behind the south shore: the whole lake across the frame, the herd along the waterline below, the far cliffs and caves, the brow rising to the top right.
eye-01.end: 88 m past the key position and 31 m above the water, over the amber shallows: the herd has passed under the frame and the deep water is nearer and wider.
eye-01.move: A level glide toward the lake, 176 m in 3.6 s, drifting 44 m to the right, through the establishing view at frame 8412.
eye-01.focus: On the far edge of the deep.

eye-02.start: 1.1 m above the shallows: the amber mats combed toward the centre of the lake, one drinker on the left, the far cliffs behind.
eye-02.end: 10 m to the right and 11 m forward, 2.3 m up, turned left to keep the drinker in the frame.
eye-02.focus: On the mats a few metres ahead of the lens.

eye-03.start: 1.7 m up at the lip where the floor of the shallows stops: the lip runs away to the left with the deep beyond it and the skeleton lies on it.
eye-03.end: 6.6 m to the left and 6 m forward, turned right to keep the skeleton in the frame.

eye-04.start: 1.9 m up on the south shore, on a long lens, 3.6 m left of the key position and panned 8 degrees right of it: three drinkers and a calf on the left, rings on the water at their mouths.
eye-04.end: 1.2 m right of the key position and 2 m back, panned 3 degrees left of it, with the track at rest. A nearer animal has come in at the right edge as a foreground shape.
eye-04.move: A lateral track along the waterline that slows all the way and is at rest on the last frame, through the key at frame 9003, with the near animals sliding against the far shore.
eye-04.focus: On the nearest of the three on the left.

eye-05.start: On a bluff on the south shore, 25.75 m up and 900 m from the centre, on a very long lens: over the necks of two drinkers, the dome of water that rises at the centre of the lake.
eye-05.end: 452 m straight above the centre of the lake, looking straight down with north at the top: deep water and the nine rings of the handoff, with 211 m of water above and below the middle of the frame. The first frame of the rise draws the same water and the same rings, so the cut cannot be seen.
eye-05.move: It holds on the key, then makes one flight in the plane through the centre of the lake: out over the water, climbing while it tilts from 1.9 degrees down to straight down and the lens opens from 8 to 50 degrees. Peak speed 292 m a second at frame 9420. The dome sinks and nine rings grow out of the centre, at rest from frame 9481. The far shore leaves by the top of the frame near frame 9400. From frame 9517 the camera is on the vertical and climbs 0.6 percent a frame, the rate the rise starts on.
eye-05.focus: On the dome at the centre, then on the water straight below.

ribs-01.start: 1500 m out to sea on the axis of the establishing picture and 8.6 m above the water: the near left rib stands as the bank in the left third, the channel between the two rows of blades runs away up the middle, the arch rock sits right of centre, and the sea runs fast under the camera.
ribs-01.end: 71 m short of the establishing position and 1.9 m above the tidal floor, already over the wet sand, with the weed wall of the near left rib filling the left third and still travelling at 29 m a second into the strait.
ribs-01.move: In. One approach of 1330 m along the line of sight of the establishing picture, heading 8 degrees east of north. It starts at 110 m a second and slows smoothly all the way; it crosses the surf line at about 12 seconds and comes down from 8.6 m to head height.
ribs-01.focus: On the channel between the rows.

ribs-02.start: The same move as ribs-01, one frame later: 70 m short of the establishing position at head height, the weed wall of the near left rib on the left and both rows of ribs running away to the horizon.
ribs-02.end: 37 m past the establishing position and 14 m to the right of it, past the near left rib, with the feeders on the wet sand ahead, travelling at 10 m a second.
ribs-02.move: In. The camera travels 113 m, slowing from 29 to 10 m a second, and passes through the establishing view at the key frame.
ribs-02.focus: On the far ribs at the key, the establishing view.

ribs-03.start: 44 m up beside the colony buttress, looking up along its ledges and the nests on them.
ribs-03.end: 28 m to the left and 6 m higher across the face of the colony.
ribs-03.focus: On the ledges at the centre of the frame.

ribs-04.start: 2 m above the floor on a long lens: three feeders on the wet sand, with the bore a white line on the horizon.
ribs-04.end: 29 m closer, on the nearest feeder with its head down.

ribs-05.start: Low on the floor, 30 m back from the weed wall of the near left rib.
ribs-05.end: Close under the drowned one, hanging head down on the weed about 10 m up, with the flat and the far ribs on the right.

ribs-06.start: 0.9 m above the floor between two weed stacks, looking down the strait: the bore comes through the gate 120 m ahead.
ribs-06.end: 12 m back, and the wall of water fills the frame.
ribs-06.focus: On the front of the bore.

spine-01.start: 150 m back along the crest and 34 m up, in the first strike: the first spire, the mouth of the canal below it, the tracks in the snow, and the ridge curving right toward the band of last light.
spine-01.end: 44 m past the key position and 6 m above the snow, closing on the mouth of the canal.

spine-02.start: 102 m off the lee edge of the first spire, three quarters of the way up it: the rock face fills the left half, the holdfasts sit on its edge, the ribbons of the kites stream right, the band of last light shows between them.
spine-02.end: 62 m from the edge, 40 m to the right and 44 m forward along the ribbons. The rock face has slid off to the left edge, the holdfasts are 1.6 times larger, and the far spires and the storm show through the ribbons.
spine-02.focus: On the holdfasts and the nearest ribbons.

spine-03.start: 11 m back from the dead ridge-runner, 3.2 m up: the carcass small in the middle, the tracks leading to the mouth of the canal, the first spire and the ridge behind.
spine-03.end: The key framing, held: the carcass low in the middle and right of the frame, its quills at the left end and a clawed foreleg toward the lens, the mouth of the canal and the ridge above it.
spine-03.move: It reaches the key and then creeps 0.2 m further: it stops short of the carcass, which never grows past its size at the key.

spine-04.start: 1664 m from the tip of the third spire, past the fin of the second spire, which fills the left third. The strike lands three frames before the key.
spine-04.end: 1407 m from the tip. The third spire and its ribbons are 1.18 times larger, and the fin of the second spire has slid against them toward the left edge. A second strike on the last frame.
spine-04.focus: On the tip of the third spire.

spine-05.start: Inside the canal, 35 m from its far mouth and facing it: the sleepers small on the left wall, one animal standing ahead near the mouth, and through the opening the storm, the band of last light and the far spires.
spine-05.end: 22 m from the far mouth. The sleepers have slid off the left edge, the opening is 1.6 times larger, and the standing animal has walked 4 m away from the camera toward the mouth.
spine-05.move: A steady push along the canal toward its far mouth. Nothing crosses the lens.
spine-05.focus: On the herd, with the mouth beyond it soft.
